title: Lower Bound for Affine-Quadratic Self-Equivalences of Permuted Modular Addition
summary: Subsets of the conjectured cardinality are constructed for word sizes 5–64, but the claimed universal lower bound from word size 4 onward remains open.

formal_statement.body: For word sizes $5 \le n \le 64$, a construction yields a subset of affine-quadratic self-equivalences of permuted modular addition with cardinality $3^2\cdot 2^{3n+14}-3\cdot 2^{2n+8}$. Determine whether, for every word size $n\ge 4$, the total number of such self-equivalences is at least $3^2\cdot 2^{3n+14}-3\cdot 2^{2n+8}$; that is, prove or refute this conjectured universal lower bound.

scope.domain: Algebraic study of affine-quadratic self-equivalences of permuted modular addition.
parameters: n: word size appearing in the range and cardinality bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute whether the stated lower bound holds for every word size n at least 4.

citations.label: Implicit White-Box Implementations: White-Boxing ARX Ciphers

progress.summary: The source constructs subsets of the stated cardinality for word sizes 5–64 and explicitly conjectures that the same expression lower-bounds the total number of self-equivalences for every word size at least 4.
